subtitle: Lesson 7 · T-SQL Foundations

code:
SELECT Name,
  CASE Color
    WHEN 'Red' THEN 'Warm'
    WHEN 'Blue' THEN 'Cool'
    ELSE 'Other'
  END AS ColorGroup
FROM Production.Product;
caption: SQL Server checks Color against each WHEN in order — first match wins.

eyebrow: It's an expression, not a statement
code:
SELECT Name, Size,
  CASE Size
    WHEN 'S' THEN 'Small'
    WHEN 'M' THEN 'Medium'
    WHEN 'L' THEN 'Large'
    ELSE 'Unspecified'
  END AS SizeCategory
FROM Production.Product;
caption: CASE produces one value per row — just like the aliased expressions from Lesson 5.

subtitle: When you need real conditions, not just exact matches.
